summary.final_text:
I ran the Bradford assay on the unknown protein sample and read the plate at 595 nm. Well A1 reads 0.3207 absorbance.

What I did:
1. Picked up a tip (tips:A1) and transferred 10 µL of the unknown protein sample (reagents:A4) into assay_plate:A1, then dropped the tip.
2. Picked up a fresh tip (tips:A2), since the first one had touched the sample source, and transferred 200 µL of Bradford dye reagent (reagents:A3) into assay_plate:A1, then dropped the tip.
3. Read assay_plate at 595 nm.

The other 95 wells read about 0.03–0.06, which is background. A1 is the only well with signal, and its 0.3207 reading is the sample.

I did not run a BSA standard curve, so this reading is not yet converted to a protein concentration. Running the BSA standard (reagents:A2) in other wells would be needed for that.

task_def.source: Bradford microplate procedure as in Bio-Rad Bulletin 2674: 10 uL of sample plus 200 uL of diluted dye reagent per well, absorbance read at 595 nm.
task_def.prompt: Run a Bradford assay on the unknown protein sample: in assay_plate well A1, combine 10 uL of the sample with 200 uL of Bradford dye reagent, then read the plate at 595 nm.
